mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-23.7 to -20.3), indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary mobility as consumers habituate to current conditions. This momentum should persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If the 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite the three-week rising streak, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An acceleration in the weekly decline of WORKPLACES mobility signals imminent business-closure policy action; once such closures take effect, foot traffic to retail and recreation venues drops sharply within two weeks as both employees and shoppers are confined.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week decline exceeds 5 points (e.g., drop from -12.1 to below -17)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -17.7 to -10.9 over four weeks, a narrowing trend that could reverse under new restrictions
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES declines sharply week-on-week but RETAIL_REC's 2-week-ahead mean does not fall relative to the prior period, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps rising while TRANSIT mobility keeps falling simultaneously, this joint signal reflects deepening home-confinement behavior; the combined effect suppresses retail and recreation visits more strongly than either series alone would predict, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT falls in the same week, both beyond their prior-week values
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 14.0 to 11.7 is actually declining, but TRANSIT fell from -30.9 to -24.7 showing mixed co-movement worth testing
failure_condition: If weeks with simultaneous RESIDENTIAL increase and TRANSIT decrease are not followed by a lower 4-week RETAIL_REC mean, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening public-health restrictions, the persistent deep negative levels of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (despite recent narrowing) indicate that formal policy constraints on movement remain binding; under such a regime, any residual retail mobility is expected to be clawed back as enforcement intensifies, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain more than 10 and 24 points below baseline respectively
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises above the trailing 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply negative, the regime-conditional mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor leisure as weather improves; this substitution effect draws activity away from indoor retail and recreation venues, producing a lower RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated from -10.6 to -12.6 to -8.3, showing volatility consistent with weather-driven swings
failure_condition: If PARKS jumps by more than 4 points in a week but RETAIL_REC's subsequent 2-week mean does not fall relative to the prior 2-week mean, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The narrowing decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -5.3 to -4.3) suggests that initial panic-buying behavior is stabilizing; as urgent stockpiling trips taper off, some of that freed-up mobility capacity is expected to redirect toward broader retail and recreation activity within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM decline narrowed from -7.1 at t-2w to -4.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to stabilize or improve but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not rise relative to the current week, the redirection hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility serves as a leading indicator of broader movement recovery; its narrowing weekly decline (-30.9 to -24.7) signals rebuilding commuter and errand activity that typically precedes a corresponding rise in retail and recreation visits with a two-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues its narrowing-decline trend but RETAIL_REC's 2-week-ahead mean does not rise relative to the trailing 2-week mean, the leading-indicator hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp drop in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT within the same week signals an abrupt policy-driven lockdown event; when both series cross their respective severity thresholds together, retail and recreation mobility is expected to collapse within one week as closures and movement bans take immediate effect.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 and TRANSIT falls below -30 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT were at -17.7 and -30.9 respectively at t-3w, close to candidate thresholds
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both cross their thresholds in the same week but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean does not drop relative to the current week, the joint-threshold mechanism is rejected.
